messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 2 error: 'DAYL5HOUR' not found
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I saw a similar error earlier today which was the result of a user masking all the data and then expecting GGIR to still run meaningful analysis. In the case earlier today the solution was to set maxdur = 0.

Further, did you try running GGIR with default parameters and did you inspect the pdf file in the result/QC folder? Often this gives a good idea of whether there is data to be processed.

That said, I just prepare a draft update to GGIR that avoid the error. Could you please try it out:

library(remotes)
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issues_1179_1180")

Thanks,
Vincent

Hi James,

This error is actually produced by the verisense code and not by GGIR.

Verisense code is not actively maintained. I previously left some suggestions in their repository to update the code:
https://github.com/ShimmerEngineering/Verisense-Toolbox/issues/9
https://github.com/ShimmerEngineering/Verisense-Toolbox/issues/8

Do either of these suggestions address your issue?

If not, I am happy to investigate your issues as a paid consultancy and as part of the process try to tidy up the use of Verisense algorithm, please send me a direct message if you are interested.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

On Monday, 22 July 2024 at 10:46 PM, Jiaxin “Grace” Chen <rusc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear colleagues,
>
> When processing our actigraphy data using GGIR, we noticed that a number of raw data files (about 15 out of 155) generated an error message during Part 4:
> "Error in if (is.na <http://is.na>(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero”
>
> After some investigation, we traced the error message back to function g.sib.det(). See below our processes and proposed solution:
> The printed error message occurred in line 297 in g.part4.R
> The issue is from the variable defaultGuiderOnset having a NULL value (which results in is.na <http://is.na>(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE to have length 0).
> To find out why the variable defaultGuiderOnset is NULL, we noted that it takes its value from SPTE_start[j], as assigned on line 292.
> SPTE_start came from the meta.sleep.folder, which contains RData outputs generated by function g.part3().
> We compared the milestone 3 files from data files that ran successfully and files that failed and observed that in the data frame "sib.cla.sum," files that failed contained the value 0 in the night variable, while files that ran to completion had night indexes starting at 1.
> We looked at the g.part3.R file to find out where the values for the variable night were generated.
> The data frame "sib.cla.sum" is created by the function g.sib.sum() in line 118, and this function requires an input parameter "SLE."
> SLE was generated using the function g.sib.det() in line 82.
> From here, we looked at g.sib.det.R.
> The variable night is initialized in line 116 to contain the value of 0.
> These values were later modified according to another variable, sptei, which was initialized as 0 in line 221.
> We believe the problem lies in lines 230 and 231, where nights containing data under 60 epochs were skipped, and the sptei was not updated in the next line (i.e., at this point, for these nights, sptei == 0).
> It follows that, for nights under 60 epochs, the variable night will have a value of 0.
> So, in g.part4.R, when the defaultGuiderOnset variable is set to SPTE_start[j], where “j” is the location index in the list nnights.list (line 265) and that a location index of 0 will result in NULL values, we know the following:
> min(sib.cla.sum$night) == 0, for these problematic files
> (lines 216-217) first_night = min(sib.cla.sum$night)
> last_night = max(sib.cla.sum$night)
> (line 219) nnightlist = first_night:last_night
> (line 226) nnights.list = nnightlist
> Since “j” will be of value 0 in the first iteration of the for-loop starting at line 265, we will see SPTE_start[j] == NULL, and consequently, defaultGuiderOnset == NULL.
> In our specific cases, we can address this issue by running GGIR() separately for input data files that crashed due to this error by skipping their first night in part 4 (by adding the argument "excludefirst.part4 = TRUE" to GGIR()). However, for replicability purposes, it is not ideal that these input files will be run using a slightly different shell script than the rest of the inputs.
>
> We wanted to share these with the rest of the GGIR community in case anyone else has run into a similar issue. If helpful, we would also like to propose a potential fix in the source code so that this won't be an issue for future projects:
> In file g.sib.det.R OR g.sib.sum.R, whichever is more convenient and appropriate, consider implementing a change such that the final output is free of rows in which night is equal to 0.
> Sample code: df <- df %>% filter(night !=0), where df is the name of the output data frame ("metatmp" or "sib.cla.sum," depending on where the change is implemented).
> The reason why we think this fix might work is because the nights with night = 0 are, by design and reason of too little data, to be skipped. Therefore, dropping those rows should not be a major cause of concern.
> We hope some of you might find this information helpful -- thanks!
>
> Best,
> Grace

GGIR(datadir = "Volumes/test/countdata",
     outputdir = "/Volumes/test/converted_output_withdiary",
     dataFormat="actiwatch_csv",
     extEpochData_timeformat="%d/%m/%Y%H:%M:%S",
     mode=1:5,
     do.report=c(2,4,5),
     idloc=2, #default is 1, but with idloc=2 GGIR looks at the filename and extracts the character string preceding the first occurance of a "_"
     windowsizes=c(30, 900,3600),#30istheexpectedepochlength
     visualreport=FALSE,
     outliers.only=FALSE,
     HASIB.algo="ColeKripke1992",

     sleepefficiency.metric = 2,

As we discussed during the GGIR training you should never store files in the directory specified with parameter datadir. GGIR attempts to read any file that is in there under the assumption that it is an accelerometer data file.

Sleep diaries are not generated by an accelerometer and should therefore never be stored in the same folder as the accelerometer data. You can store them anywhere you like as long as it is not the datadir location and ideally also not inside the output directory generated by GGIR.

Best,

Vincent

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Energy expenditure
messages.body_plain:
Hi Martinique,

Most of the energy prediction models are linear models, because there is no evidence that it needs to be non-linear. If you apply the same linear model to all your data then that by definition does not add information.

As a metaphor: if you multiply everyone's age by 2 and add 10 years then the new age variable will be equally correlated with any other measure of their anthropology or health compared with the initial age variable. We should not fool ourselves to think that we are measuring something different.

Secondly, attempting to estimate energy expenditure comes with most of the challenges I listed for MET in https://www.accelting.com/updates/why-does-ggir-facilitate-cut-points/. That blog post is about estimating time spent in ranges of energy expenditure but the problems are largely the same for estimating energy expenditure as a continuous outcomes.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Dear Aaron,

An Actiwatch example file snippet that GGIR uses for testing can be found here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/inst/testfiles/Actiwatch.csv

It seems that this does not match the format you have created, which probably explains why GGIR cannot make sense of it.

Other facilitated data formats can be found here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/tree/master/inst/testfiles

I would not be surprised if Actiwatch like most other accelerometer manufacturers generated many variations on their csv format being oblivious to the burden to research.
Also, I think the issue is that the term Actiwatch has been used by multiple brands, so it might be that we are referring to a different Actiwatch brand. I think the one I have worked with used to be provided by Phillips.

So far, I have only implemented functionality for the csv formats that people have paid me to implement. If you want more data formats to work then there are three options:
You prepare an enhancement to GGIR and make a pull request in GitHub, which I am then happy to review and merge.
You hire me or someone else to make these enhancement.
You wait for someone else in this google group to reply and work on it for free.

Alternatively, your best chance may be to modify your data format to match any of the data formats currently facilitated by GGIR.

Best wishes, Vincent

remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue1191_ami_motionlogger")

GGIR(datadir = datadir,
     outputdir = outputdir,
     mode = 1:5,
     overwrite = TRUE,
     windowsizes = c(60, 900, 3600),
     threshold.in <http://threshold.in> = 1.5,
     threshold.mod = 3,
     threshold.vig = 6,
     dataFormat = "ami_csv",
     extEpochData_timeformat = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S",
     HASPT.algo = "NotWorn",
     acc.metric = "ExtAct",
     desiredtz = "America/New_York",
     overwrite = TRUE,
     do.report = c(2, 4, 5),
     visualreport = FALSE)

For me this runs but I see that without access to sleep diary GGIR is not good yet at guessing the main resting period by which the sleep analyses is not informative. However, if that could be fixed then this may work.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jessica,

GGIR facilitates this with parameter maxRecordingInterval <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#maxrecordinginterval>
For example, if you set this to 24, GGIR will append all recordings with the same participant ID that have a gap in between them of less than 24 hours.

The number of recordings to be merged is not limited, so technically you can have a whole year of recordings, which are then merged into one recording. Because this would be too much data to merge at raw level the merging happens at epoch level in GGIR part 1.

Best, Vincent
